I farm 13.1 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will put the full 13.1 mu into winter wheat first and then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. I have 30 years of experience, only two people in the household, and I have well irrigation, so I will keep to a steady, practical plan that I know I can manage well. For wheat, I will use improved seed, do rotary tillage after the maize season, apply moderate fertilizer with more nitrogen than phosphorus and potassium, and irrigate three times because wheat in my area responds well to water at key stages. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it is what I trust for stable yield, and I will reduce tillage pressure by using no-tillage after wheat harvest so I can sow quickly and save labor. I will still fertilize maize well, but with slightly less irrigation than wheat because the rainy season helps. I will keep pesticide use to a normal working level for weeds, insects, and disease pressure, aiming for stable yield instead of taking unnecessary risk.
